prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Hafnium (하프늄) itself — the sovereign of the Hafnium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: early thirties — a poised, graceful face with soft contours; at most faint lines, no deep folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: a quiet melancholy; olive skin; oval face; smaller, narrower eyes than usual anime proportion — hooded eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; low heavy brows; petite straight nose; full heart-shaped lips; near-black obsidian eyes; smoky dark eye makeup.
Body and hair: pear-shaped and curvaceous — slimmer shoulders over a narrow waist, full rounded hips and thick thighs, a full bust build; long hair swept to one side over a shaved undercut with long bangs falling over one eye; cool gunmetal-silver hair, darker underneath as if cast in its own shadow, with a faint blue-black sheen.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: a quiet, thoughtful look, lips lightly closed.
Her element, carried in her design: hafnium: a heavy, lustrous steel-grey metal so chemically identical to its twin zirconium that it hid unseen inside every zirconium ore for well over a century, until 1923, when X-ray spectra taken in Copenhagen revealed its lines exactly where atomic theory said they must be, and it was named for Hafnia, the old Latin name of that harbour city; where zirconium lets neutrons pass, hafnium swallows them, so it makes the control rods that hold a reactor in check; it is nearly twice as dense as its twin; its oxide, a few atoms thick, guards the switches inside chips, and its carbide survives some of the fiercest heat known.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: one large brass mechanical gauntlet covering a whole arm over an otherwise trim outfit — the contrast makes the shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: shadowed gunmetal silver, cold blue-black, pale X-ray blue, neutron-dark steel.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: in 1923, the X-ray laboratory of a theoretical physics institute in Copenhagen: glass X-ray tubes aimed at targets coated with zirconium ore powder, photographic plates on which hidden spectral lines first appeared, tall windows over canals and green copper roofs.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Hf) and atomic number (72) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
